name: Centene
description: Centene is a government-focused health insurer: states pay it to run Medicaid managed care (57 percent of 2025 revenue, 12.5 million members), the federal government pays for Medicare plans (19 percent, including the largest stand-alone Part D drug plan business with 8.1 million members) and ACA Marketplace plans sold as Ambetter (the rest of Commercial, 5.5 million members, largely subsidised by federal premium tax credits). It collects a premium per member and pays the medical bills. Its own 10-K calls it the nation's largest Medicaid and Marketplace insurer by publicly available membership data. 2025 was a loss year: a $7.3 billion impairment charge (mostly $6.7 billion goodwill) and Marketplace pricing errors turned a $3.3 billion profit into a $6.7 billion net loss, followed by recovery in the first half of 2026.

businessLines.name: Medicaid
businessLines.how: States pay fixed monthly rates per enrollee, set by the state each year; Centene pays the medical claims and keeps the gap, so profit depends on state rate adequacy and members' medical cost trends.
businessLines.description: State-contracted Medicaid managed care (TANF, expansion, CHIP, foster care, aged/blind/disabled, long-term care) in many states, including Iowa Health Link from July 2025.

revenue.note: FY2024 101,417 (+9%). Includes premium tax revenue. Medicaid membership 12,518,400 at 2025-12-31 vs 13,003,500 (traditional 10,932,600; high acuity 1,585,800).

operatingProfit.note: Gross margin (premium and service revenues less medical costs and cost of services), the segment profit measure reported; FY2024 6,246 (-9%). Share is of consolidated gross margin $14,209M. Operating earnings by segment are not reported.

businessLines.name: Medicare
businessLines.how: CMS pays a monthly amount per Medicare Advantage or PDP member (risk-adjusted), plus members pay premiums for some plans; Centene pays drug and medical claims. Part D plans carry high revenue per member relative to margin.
businessLines.description: Medicare Advantage (largely under the Wellcare brand, across 32 states), Medicare Supplement and the stand-alone Medicare Part D prescription drug plan (PDP).

revenue.note: FY2024 23,032 (+62%, driven by Part D PDP growth). Medicare (MA and Supplement) members 1,002,600 vs 1,110,900; Medicare PDP members 8,118,600 vs 6,925,700.

businessLines.name: Commercial
businessLines.how: Individuals buy plans on the ACA exchanges, most of the premium paid by federal premium tax credits (subsidies, whose rules changed under the 2025 budget law from 2026); Centene pays claims and receives or pays a risk-adjustment transfer based on how sick its members are relative to the market.
businessLines.description: ACA Health Insurance Marketplace plans sold as Ambetter Health (29 states at 2025-12-31), plus off-exchange individual, ICHRA (Ambetter Health Solutions) and commercial group plans.

revenue.note: FY2024 33,702 (+25%). Marketplace members 5,541,400 vs 4,382,100; individual and commercial group 452,500 vs 431,400.
